column3: The Weaver and the Hound
column5: After the death of a skilled weaver named Knowles from Dean Combe, his ghost appears weaving at his loom until a priest forces him to leave. As punishment for his worldly desires, the weaver's spirit is transformed into a hound and condemned to an eternal task at Hound's Pool.

column3: The Gwyllgi, Or Dog Of Darkness.
column5: The frightful apparition of a mastiff with blazing red eyes, known as the Gwyllgi, haunted Pant y Madog near Laugharne, Carmarthenshire, terrifying a woman named Rebecca Adams as it approached her and emitted an earth-shaking scream. This spectral dog is said to still haunt Carmarthenshire, as reported by witnesses in Llangynog who have seen such apparitions.

column3: A Familiar Spirit In The Shape Of A Dog And The Lonely Night Traveller.
column5: A man from Cilcwm was returning home late at night through a lonely mountainous area when he encountered a friendly black dog walking beside him. Upon reaching home, the dog mysteriously vanished, leading the man to believe it was a familiar spirit sent by a wizard to keep him company on his journey.

column3: Owd Rugman of Attlebridge
column5: A shaggy phantom hound known as Owd Rugman haunted the rural lanes and villages of Attlebridge and Lenwade during the late nineteenth century. Local residents reported numerous frightening encounters with this spectral beast as it roamed the countryside.

column3: The Bexwell Shuck and the Rector's Hound
column5: Around 1870, the Bexwell parish clerk encountered a terrifying black dog vanishing through a hedge with a loud rattling of chains and a smell of sulphur along the road to Downham Market. Although the local rector suggested the beast was simply his own escaped hound, he was left entirely puzzled by the supernatural stench.

column3: The Phantom Newfoundland of Roudham Heath
column5: A motorist driving across Roudham Heath late at night encountered a gigantic, supernatural Newfoundland dog crossing the ancient Peddar's Way. Upon returning home, his mother immediately recognized the apparition as Old Shuck.

column3: The Guardian Hound of Catfield Marshes
column5: While illegally gathering rushes on the marshes near Catfield Hall, a group of women fleeing a gamekeeper were guided safely home by a mysterious black dog.

column3: The Phantom Hound of Coltishall Bridge
column5: Multiple residents and travellers have reported encountering a massive, silent black dog with glowing eyes lurking around Coltishall Bridge after dark. Over the decades, terrified witnesses have watched the monstrous phantom hound materialize, cross their path, and vanish into thin air.

column3: The Hateful Thing of Geldeston
column5: A woman walking back to Geldeston along the market path with her daughter and her companion encounters a terrifying, shapeshifting beast. The entity trails them before finally disappearing up the sandy lane leading to the churchyard.

column3: Black Shuck of Weasenham Lanes
column5: While staying at her late great aunt's cottage in Weasenham, a recovering librarian is pursued by the spectral black hound Black Shuck along the misty autumn lanes near Weasenham Woods.

column3: The Halvergate Shuck Encounter
column5: During a severe November storm in 2000, a motorist driving across the marshes near Acle witnessed a gigantic, wolf-like spectral hound with burning red eyes pacing his vehicle. Another similar midnight encounter on the Acle Straight was later recounted by student researchers interviewing local witnesses.

column3: The Christmas Eve Apparition at Temple Bar
column5: A late-night winter traveler walking home to Earsham witnessed a large black hound emerge from a private estate, cross the road, and vanish directly through a rectory wall without leaving any footprints in the snow.

column3: The Shipwreck Hound of Bacton Abbey
column5: A colossal, shaggy spectral dog said to originate from an ancient shipwreck paces back and forth along the coast road between Bacton Abbey and Beeston Regis with glaring, luminous eyes. Local tradition connects the phantom hound to men buried at the historic abbey ruins.

column3: The Ghostly Shuck Dog of Clip Street Lane
column5: A grandmother witnessed a ghostly Shuck Dog just outside her bungalow on a green lane in Bale. The spectral hound's appearance was preserved as a vivid family memory.

column3: The Guardian Hound of Bawburgh
column5: While cycling home late at night, a young man encountered a colossal spectral hound sitting by a village signpost before an unlit vehicle seemingly crashed into it and vanished. The supernatural encounter was later believed by the witness to have miraculously saved his life.

column3: The Spectral Hound of Beeston Heath
column5: A terrifying headless spectral dog with flaming saucer eyes rises from the sea at Beeston to prowl along Shock's Lane toward Overstrand churchyard every evening at twilight.

column3: The Ghost Dog of Beeston Bump
column5: A terrifying spectral hound known as Old Shuck patrols the North Norfolk coast between Beeston and Overstrand every evening, heralded by glowing saucer-shaped eyes and smelling of brimstone. This phantom dog serves as both a fearful premonition of coastal storms and a guardian of the crumbling cliff paths.

column3: The Cyclist and the Hound of Bergh Apton
column5: Returning home from a darts match late at night near the end of the Second World War, a cyclist was ambushed by Black Shuck near a roadside pond. The snarling hound lunged at crossbar height before miraculously vanishing into a solid wall.

column3: The Tinkling Chain of Cley Hill
column5: Walking home along the A149 from Cley to Blakeney at midnight, a woman is stalked up a hill by an invisible presence dragging a chain. She hears the unseen entity pass down Back Lane before fleeing down the High Street.

column3: The Black Hound of Blickling Hall
column5: Following his death, the corpse of an unpopular Blickling baronet was repeatedly rejected by the consecrated earth before transforming into a terrifying spectral black dog that plagued the estate. The beast was eventually subdued by a London wizard and imprisoned within the south-east turret of Blickling Hall.

column3: Old Scarfe's Haunt
column5: The ancient stone walls of a Roman fort are haunted by a demonic one-eyed hellhound named Old Scarfe. This spectral beast is said to be the reincarnation of a deeply wicked 13th-century knight.

column3: The Phantom Hound of Coltishall Bridge
column5: Black Shuck, the legendary ghostly black hound of East Anglia, is frequently sighted as a silent, massive beast near Coltishall Bridge and vanishing into thin air on Coltishall High Street.

column3: The Shuck of Old Costessey
column5: A mysterious spectral black dog, known as a Shuck, was reported roaming around a village pub in Old Costessey. The unsettling apparition added to the rich folklore of ghostly hounds in East Anglia.

column3: The Faithful Phantom of Cromer Pier
column5: A ghostly black dog haunts the shoreline near Cromer Pier, eternally gazing out to sea and vanishing into thin air when approached.

column3: The Christmas Eve Apparition at Temple Bar
column5: A late-night winter traveler walking home to Earsham witnessed a large black hound emerge from a private estate, cross the road, and vanish directly through a rectory wall without leaving any footprints in the snow.

column3: The Spectral Hound of Felbrigg Woods
column5: Black Shuck, the legendary devil dog with glowing red eyes, is said to roam the ancient woods and grounds surrounding Felbrigg House as a fatal omen. Encountering the spectral hound in this North Norfolk estate forewarns of death before the year is out.

column3: The Hound of Poppylot Road
column5: A cyclist traveling along Poppylot Road at midnight in the 1930s encountered a massive black hound with glowing green eyes that was dragging a heavy rattling chain.

column3: The Demon Hound of Saint Mary's
column5: The abandoned ruins of an eleventh-century church in Fulmodeston are haunted by Black Shuck, a terrifying demon hound said to roam near the site. Local lore also speaks of an unburied coffin beneath the rubble whose occupant wanders the derelict grounds.

column3: The Vanishing Dog of Chancel Lane
column5: A witness walking past Garveston church in broad daylight watched a dark, shaggy dog trot across an open field before it abruptly vanished into thin air.

column3: The Highway Phantom of Geldeston
column5: A terrifying spectral black dog as large as a horse once stalked lone travellers along the road from Geldeston to Bungay, growling fiercely and dragging victims by their clothing.

column3: The Phantom Hound of All Saints
column5: In 1913, a late-night cyclist narrowly avoided crashing into a spectral dog near a ruined church tower in Gillingham before the creature vanished into the graveyard.

column3: The Coastguard's Phantom Hound
column5: In April 1972, a coastguard on duty early in the morning witnessed a large black hound suddenly appear and vanish on the beach north of the Gorleston rescue headquarters.

column3: The Demon Dog of Peddar's Way
column5: The legendary East Anglian hell-hound Black Shuck is said to haunt the ancient trackway of Peddar's Way as it passes through the countryside surrounding Great Bircham. This spectral demon dog is famously mirrored in the stone carvings of St Mary's Church within the village.

column3: The Phantom Hound of Peddar's Way
column5: An 18-year-old scout on a night hike along Peddar's Way was suddenly confronted by a massive black spectral hound that leaped toward him before mysteriously vanishing. Exactly one year later, the witness suffered a near-fatal accident, fulfilling the local omen associated with sighting the beast.

column3: The White Hound of Great Snoring
column5: In the years preceding the Second World War, a ghostly white dog was frequently seen darting across the road connecting Great Snoring and Little Snoring, culminating in an encounter where an unsuspecting motorist drove straight through its spectral form.

column3: The Demonic Hound of Old Scarfe
column5: A depraved 13th-century baron was transformed by the Devil into a fiery-eyed, chained hellhound that haunts Southtown Road and the vaults of a local inn. To this day, the spectral beast terrorizes benighted travelers with sorrowful moans and clanking chains.

column3: The Spectral Hound of Gresham Cross
column5: Cyclists returning from Gresham in the late 1930s encountered an enormous, silent black dog emerging suddenly from heavy sea mist near the Old Stone Cross.

column3: The Halvergate Shuck Encounter
column5: In November 2000, a motorist driving past the marshes toward Halvergate during a storm was accompanied alongside his vehicle by a massive wolfhound-like spectral dog with burning red eyes.

column3: The Phantom Dog of Church Lane
column5: A witness walking along Church Lane in Hardley at dawn encountered a large, shaggy grey dog that vanished mysteriously into the barley fields.

column3: The Vanishing Hound of Market Hole
column5: A young cyclist returning home late at night nearly collided with a massive spectral dog that suddenly materialized on a country road before vanishing into thin air.

column3: The Faines
column5: Calf-sized spectral creatures with glowing saucer eyes and giant silent black dogs haunt the roads and playing fields of Hethersett. Witnesses have reported these phantom hounds padding alongside cyclists before vanishing into thin air.

column3: The Phantom Dog of Kelling
column5: While pushing his bicycle along a moonlit road toward Kelling, a local man encountered a gigantic, shaggy black dog that walked silently past him and vanished through a closed gate. When he recounted the event to villagers the next day, they identified the beast as Old Shuck.

column3: The Phantom Hound of the Links
column5: A spectral dog has been reported haunting the fairways of the Old Hunstanton golf course. Local folklore and regional surveys explicitly distinguish this apparition from the infamous Black Shuck.

column3: The Phantom Dog of Buxton Lamas Church
column5: A gentleman encountering a large black shaggy dog outside a Norfolk church in 1930 attempts to pet the beast, only for it to vanish into thin air just as his brother passes away in hospital.

column3: The Phantom Hound of the Airfield
column5: During the early months of the Second World War, an airman on duty near Methwold encountered a colossal supernatural hound lurking amongst the trees. The terrifying apparition was recognized by servicemen as a massive, otherworldly beast.

column3: The Phantom Dog of Neatishead
column5: A local resident walking home after dark in Neatishead encountered a spectral black dog that proved to be entirely incorporeal when kicked.

column3: The Two-Headed Beast of Northrepps Cottage
column5: A terrifying two-headed spectral hound and shape-shifting phantom haunted a sunken tree-arched lane behind a historic Norfolk cottage, while a later owner encountered a massive black dog inside his own cellar. Local smugglers also utilized the legend to ward off unwanted nighttime visitors.

column3: The Smugglers' Phantom Hound of Old Hunstanton
column5: Smugglers in Old Hunstanton exploited the local legend of the spectral dog Old Shuck by attaching lanterns to black rams to frighten away curious villagers during contraband runs.

column3: The Phantom Hound of RAF Oulton
column5: During World War Two, an airman walking to his military station in Oulton encountered a silent, spectral black dog standing in the moonlight near Blickling Hall before it vanished into thin air.

column3: The Twilight Prowler of Overstrand Churchyard
column5: At twilight each evening, a massive spectral hound with glowing saucer eyes and a tangible shaggy coat paces along the coastal route toward Overstrand churchyard. A local gamekeeper once swore the phantom creature brushed directly beneath his hand, leaving behind scorched earth and the scent of brimstone.

column3: The One-Eyed Hound of Salhouse
column5: A gigantic spectral hound sporting a single blazing eye in the middle of its forehead terrorized the Norfolk countryside around Salhouse. Local youths bravely ventured out at night armed only with sticks to hunt the terrifying beast, to the horror of villagers who expected them to meet certain death.

column3: The Resident Hound of St. Martin's
column5: For decades, the spectral black dog known as Black Shuck made the abandoned ruins of St. Martin's Church in Sidestrand its permanent home. Glowing with fiery eyes, the legendary beast haunted the clifftop churchyard until restoration efforts disturbed its lair in the early twentieth century.

column3: The Spectral Wolf of Southery
column5: A monstrous wolf-hound sent to guard monks in the Fens turned feral, leaving behind an unworldly offspring whose spectral ghost returns every year to howl near the village church on May 29th.

column3: The Shadow in the Marsh
column5: While spending the night on the Stiffkey saltmarshes to investigate local legends, an author is stalked and pursued back to his lodging by a terrifying spectral hound.

column3: Old Shocks on the Lane to Flordon
column5: Locals became convinced they had witnessed a spectral phantom known as "Old Shocks" haunting the pathway between Tasburgh and Flordon railway station. The apparition was regarded with superstitious dread by those traveling the rural lane.

column3: The Phantom Companion of Beacon Hill Farm
column5: During the pre-First World War era, a woman walking near Beacon Hill Farm House encountered a spectral black dog that vanished into thin air upon being touched. When she reached down to pat the creature, her hand passed straight through its body.

column3: The Spectral Hound of Warren Lodge
column5: A glowing-eyed spectral hound prowls the grounds and ruins of a 15th-century gamekeeper's lodge near Thetford, filling the surrounding woodland with eerie howls.

column3: The Phantom Dog of St Mary's
column5: An old man and his spectral black dog haunt the rural paths around the ruined church, causing herds of cattle to part in startled silence as they pass.

column3: The Phantom Hound of Toft Monks
column5: While walking through the rural lanes of Toft Monks, a traveller is warned by a local woodman about the presence of Black Shuck, a spectral demon dog as large as a calf. The phantom hound is said to roam the lonely paths and marshes of the Norfolk countryside without making a sound.

column3: The Hound of Anchor Street
column5: Two teenagers exploring a woodland stream off Anchor Street in Tunstead encountered a massive, crimson-eyed spectral hound. Fearing for their lives, they fled as the terrifying creature vanished back into the trees.

column3: The Black Shuck of Weeting Castle
column5: Visitors walking around the moat of Weeting Castle have reported encountering the infamous Black Shuck, a noiseless giant black hound with a single fiery eye.

column3: The Marshland Phantom Hound
column5: While keeping vigil in the lonely marshes near Wells-next-the-Sea, a writer was stalked and nearly pounced upon by a terrifying, giant black spectral hound with glowing eyes.

column3: The Silent Phantom of West Runton Slipway
column5: In December 1972, a fisherman on the beach at West Runton encountered a gigantic, silent black dog with a broad head and small ears that paced along the base of the cliffs under the full moonlight. Despite coming within fifteen feet, the spectral beast made no sound on the shingle and cast no shadow.

column3: h The Vampire Hound of Weybourne Hoop
column5: A gigantic black hound haunts the coastal salt-lands originating from Weybourne Hoop, leaping upon benighted wayfarers to tear their throats before vanishing in smoke.

This spectral beast, known as the Bungay Black Dog, is said to haunt the lonely paths of the Suffolk Coast, silent in step but chilling in howl.

column5: The Moddey Dhoo is a spectral black dog that haunts Peel Castle on the Isle of Man. According to legend, it appeared nightly in the guardroom, vanishing into a sealed passage after terrifying an overconfident guard.

column3: Hainu
column5: Hainu is a winged dog from Japanese folklore, known for its strength, speed, and ferocity. According to legend, Hainu can be both menacing and loyal, and has been immortalized in the form of a stone monument and bronze statues in Chikugo City.
